chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman al-Sayrafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Everything that contradicts the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is to be referred back to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah.

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: The Sunnah — the practice and narrations of the Prophet (SAWW) and the Imams, the second source of Islamic law
key_terms.خَالَفَ: Contradicts/opposes — refers to any ruling, statement, or practice that goes against the Quran's explicit text or its spirit
key_terms.رُدَّ: Is to be returned/rejected — a passive imperative indicating the Sharia ruling that such contradicting matters must be referred back to and measured against scripture
key_terms.كِتَابُ اللَّهِ: The Book of Allah — the Quran, the primary and supreme source of Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about rulings that contradict the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a foundational principle of Islamic jurisprudence: any ruling, tradition, or narration that contradicts the Quran must be rejected and measured against the Quran and Sunnah. This principle was articulated in the context of marriage and divorce law — the chapter title indicates its specific application to talaq (divorce) conducted outside the Quranic framework — but its scope is universal, serving as a hermeneutical rule for Shia jurisprudence that the Quran is the supreme criterion (mizan) against which all other sources must be evaluated.
